question: Does a class-balanced, momentum-accumulated federated update beat a standard FedAvg baseline when clients hold sparse, scarce and non-IID data?
method: Simulated federated learning on the bundled breast-cancer dataset: Dirichlet label-skew partition, random feature masks per client, identical local SGD and round budget; both methods evaluated on one shared stratified hold-out test set over several seeds.
baseline: Standard FedAvg with a logistic-regression model trained by local SGD, averaged by sample count.
improved: Same local model and data, plus class-balanced local loss weights, server-side momentum (accumulative) update, and aggregation weights that down-weight clients with very few samples.
notes: Stand-in baseline/improvement inspired by accumulative learning; the Safa paper's exact update was not re-implemented. Hyperparameters were fixed a priori (no tuning, so no test-set selection). Feature scaler is fit on the pooled training split (a simplification of a real federated setting). The test set is small, so differences are noisy; only three seeds were run. Results do not test the paper's own claims or dataset.
